reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses heavily on very short, frequent easy runs, which can be beneficial for maintaining consistency, it lacks a dedicated long run or any structured hill work – crucial elements for trail running speed development. Plan B incorporates longer runs at an easy pace, simulating trail distances and building aerobic endurance, and includes a cross-training session to reduce impact and promote recovery. The inclusion of a longer run and cross-training directly addresses the goal of becoming a faster trail runner, whereas Plan A’s repetitive easy runs are unlikely to significantly improve speed without additional stimulus.
